nodes.label: Next.js Agent Rules (this is NOT the Next.js you know)
nodes.rationale: The installed Next.js version has breaking API/convention/file-structure changes relative to model training data, so agents must read node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before writing code rather than relying on memorized Next.js idioms.
nodes.norm_label: next.js agent rules (this is not the next.js you know)

nodes.label: MathUp (Hebrew RTL bagrut math-5 study platform)
nodes.rationale: Evolved from an AI-question generator into a static-first learning platform because hand-authored verified content renders at zero API cost; AI became the fallback, not the engine.
nodes.norm_label: mathup (hebrew rtl bagrut math-5 study platform)

nodes.label: Build + typecheck before every push
nodes.rationale: Push to main auto-deploys and the owner only ever views the live site, so an edit is not done until pushed. Vercel Hobby runtime differs from next dev; deploys that passed local typecheck have failed in prod and cost money.

nodes.label: Pathspec-only git commits (never git add . / -A)
nodes.rationale: The repo carries parallel work-in-progress (statistics.ts, 2020-summer-582.ts, untracked dirs); a blanket stage would sweep in-flight edits into an unrelated commit.

nodes.label: Vercel Hobby 60s serverless cap (maxDuration = 60)
nodes.rationale: Every model call must be paired with a max_tokens that fits inside 60s, otherwise the route returns nothing and still bills Anthropic — paying for a timed-out response.

nodes.label: ~$5/month Anthropic budget ceiling
nodes.rationale: Budget is tiny, so model ping-pong during bug hunts is forbidden and the $0 static-first / cache paths are preferred over any API call.

nodes.label: Prompt caching on large static system prompts (cache_control: ephemeral)
nodes.rationale: Large invariant system prompts are the cheapest thing to cache, and caching them is the main lever keeping grounded Sonnet chat inside the monthly budget.
nodes.norm_label: prompt caching on large static system prompts (cache_control: ephemeral)

nodes.label: Never put Hebrew inside KaTeX
nodes.rationale: KaTeX implements no bidi algorithm, so Hebrew inside $...$ renders reversed. Hebrew goes outside the math; subscripts use Latin letters ($m_1$, never $m_{משיק}$).

nodes.label: 5-unit bagrut math conventions (cis degrees, y²=2px, c²=a²−b²)
nodes.rationale: The Israeli MOE syllabus uses the y²=2px parabola with focus (p/2,0), not the American 4px form, and complex numbers in cis/degrees rather than e^{iθ}. Using American conventions would teach students notation the examiner does not accept.
nodes.norm_label: 5-unit bagrut math conventions (cis degrees, y2=2px, c2=a2−b2)

nodes.label: Trigonometry degrees/radians split (owner decision 2026-07-28)
nodes.rationale: trig-equations and special-angles-reduction are in degrees; trig-calculus must stay in radians because (sin x)' = cos x only holds in radians (in degrees it is (π/180)·cos x). Over-generalizing the complex-numbers 'degrees' rule to all trig once produced a wrong instruction. Guarded by scripts/verify-trig-angles.ts; verify-trig.ts hardcodes its own math and never reads content, so it cannot catch a convention regression.

nodes.label: IP boundary — no publisher solution books
nodes.rationale: Publisher solutions (יואל גבע, m-math.co.il, publisher PDFs) are copyrighted even when freely downloadable. Only MOE bagrut question text (public domain), the MOE syllabus, the model's own knowledge, and the owner's handwritten solutions are valid sources.
nodes.norm_label: ip boundary — no publisher solution books

nodes.label: Only two question types exist (MCQ + open)
nodes.rationale: The owner already evaluated and rejected drag-drop, fill-blank, match and speed-drill formats; depth comes from adding more of the two accepted types, not from inventing new interaction models.
nodes.norm_label: only two question types exist (mcq + open)

nodes.label: "Premium white" light-only design system
nodes.rationale: App is deliberately light-only with no dark-mode toggle: ivory canvas, indigo primary, gold reserved for achievements. Source of truth is app/globals.css :root, so new UI composes Tailwind plus the named utilities instead of inventing colors.

nodes.label: Dark-ink-on-light SVG diagram palette + custom-SVG-only rule
nodes.rationale: Light-on-dark stroke values are literally invisible on the ivory canvas. Diagrams must be type:'custom' raw SVG and never fn: closures, because a function crosses the RSC server→client boundary and crashes the page.
nodes.norm_label: dark-ink-on-light svg diagram palette + custom-svg-only rule

nodes.label: Monetization: free base, Pro depth (lib/access.ts)
nodes.rationale: Guided lessons and drills are static and cost $0 to serve, so they are the growth hook and must never be gated; only the Pro-depth surfaces (advanced course, archive, unlimited chat, AI photo-solve, advanced analytics) are paywalled. canAccessTopic no longer paywalls topics — topicLockReason is now purely pedagogical. There is no real billing yet: isProUser = ADMIN_EMAIL or an unset user_metadata.pro flag.

nodes.label: Static-first content architecture (zero API cost)
nodes.rationale: ~829 hand-authored, mathematically-verified questions live as TypeScript modules under content/ and render with no API call at all, which is what makes the free tier sustainable on a $5/month budget.

nodes.label: concept-quiz registry keyed `${subject}:${topic}`
nodes.rationale: Keying on topic alone is unsafe because math4 shares math5's Hebrew topic names and not always byte-identically; the composite subject:topic key makes adding a new subject one registry line.

nodes.label: Photo-scan caching: answer library first, AI last
nodes.rationale: /api/solve-photo runs cheap Sonnet-vision transcription, then matchQuestion (exact hash + Jaccard ≥0.82 over all static questions, free), then the Supabase solution_cache (free); only a true miss pays for AI text-solve, whose result is written back to the cache so the same question is never paid for twice.
nodes.norm_label: photo-scan caching: answer library first, ai last

nodes.label: localStorage-only client state (works without login, $0)
nodes.rationale: Keeping results, study plan, progress, adaptive difficulty and scans in localStorage means the product works for anonymous visitors and costs nothing to store.

nodes.label: lib/answer-check.ts deterministic mathjs grading
nodes.rationale: Grading open answers deterministically instead of via AI keeps them free. Gotchas: mathjs `log` IS natural log (write expected as log(2), not ln(2)), and trig evaluates in radians, so trig `expected` must be plain numbers/degrees or {kind:'manual'}.

nodes.label: npm run verify:content (scripts/verify-content.ts)
nodes.rationale: Supersedes check-katex-hebrew.ts because it imports the content modules instead of grepping source, so it can scope rules per field — '$= 4 - 3i$' is fine in solution.steps and a defect in keyPoints. Errors: hebrew-in-math, unbalanced $, $$display$$ mid-prose-line.

nodes.label: npm run verify:concept (shape-only gate + inventory table)
nodes.rationale: Checks SHAPE only and says so in its header — every `correct` index still has to be re-derived by hand, independently of whoever authored it. PROMOTED_TO_ERROR stays false until the 252-question target is met, because a gate that always fails gets bypassed within a day.
nodes.norm_label: npm run verify:concept (shape-only gate + inventory table)

nodes.label: verify-mcq-distinct coverage honesty ("0 problems" ≠ correct)
nodes.rationale: It skips any option containing =, <, > or Hebrew (correct — those are statements, not values), which leaves 39% coverage on the concept bank and 0% on אלגברה. It now prints per-topic coverage and names every unchecked question, and that list IS the manual-review worklist. '0 problems' means 'nothing I examined failed', not 'the data is correct'.

nodes.label: MathText single-element contract (2026-07-28)
nodes.rationale: Both modes return exactly one element (span.mathtext-inline / div.mathtext-block), each dir="rtl". Inline mode used to return a bare fragment, which let a display:flex caller turn every word and formula into its own flex item (the 'לזכור' box rendered as 3 scrambled columns). dir must be "rtl" not "auto", because KaTeX emits raw LaTeX in a clip-hidden <annotation> and auto-detection reads a Latin first-strong char, flipping Hebrew lines that open with math. Left-alignment of standalone equations is driven by a .math-only class computed from the source string, since :only-child ignores text nodes.

nodes.label: The deliberate unscoped .katex floor in globals.css
nodes.rationale: Every scoped bidi rule needs a .chat-md/.math-content ancestor, so a MathText rendered without one inherited direction:rtl from <html dir="rtl"> and showed the formula reversed. 4 of 12 call sites in /quiz had no wrapper — all in the end-of-quiz mistake review, where students read their own wrong answers backwards. The floor is intentionally soft (two declarations, no !important) so the scoped block still wins; it only removes the failure mode where nothing applies. Do not 'clean up' the apparent duplicate.
nodes.norm_label: the deliberate unscoped .katex floor in globals.css

nodes.label: Deliberate model routing (Sonnet grounded / Haiku generic)
nodes.rationale: /api/chat uses claude-sonnet-4-6 (prompt-cached) for grounded topics and claude-haiku-4-5 for generic; TUTOR_SONNET_TOPICS is a cost valve that demotes topics to Haiku if spend climbs. solve-photo needs Sonnet vision because Hebrew+LaTeX transcription is beyond Haiku. Micro-endpoints run Haiku. Question-generation routes survive only as a legacy fallback for subjects without a static bank.
nodes.norm_label: deliberate model routing (sonnet grounded / haiku generic)

nodes.label: Supabase tables created in dashboard; code degrades gracefully
nodes.rationale: Tables are created via SQL in the dashboard rather than git migrations, so a feature can ship before its table exists. Every call site wraps in try/catch and no-ops, and RLS is enforced everywhere. The owner must run the SQL before a new table's feature works live.
nodes.norm_label: supabase tables created in dashboard; code degrades gracefully

nodes.label: PROTECTED_PREFIXES middleware and the public /practice, /roadmap surfaces
nodes.rationale: /pricing, /roadmap and /practice stay public so an anonymous visitor following an old link never hits a login wall. That also makes /roadmap and /practice the only surfaces usable to verify shared rendering without a login — /quiz cannot be checked that way.
nodes.norm_label: protected_prefixes middleware and the public /practice, /roadmap surfaces

nodes.label: Strict CSP in next.config.ts (self + *.supabase.co)
nodes.rationale: Adding any external service (payment provider, Resend, etc.) requires updating connect-src/script-src or it silently breaks in production while working locally.

nodes.label: Bulk authoring: one agent per file, verify independently
nodes.rationale: Topics live in separate files so one agent per file avoids write conflicts; an authoring agent's own verification is circular, so the real checker must be re-run independently afterward.
nodes.norm_label: bulk authoring: one agent per file, verify independently

nodes.label: create-next-app bootstrap README (stock template)
nodes.rationale: Unmodified create-next-app boilerplate — documents npm run dev, editing app/page.tsx, and next/font with Geist. It has not been updated for MathUp, so CLAUDE.md is the real project documentation.

nodes.label: בר האיכות — the four-rule quality bar for every solution
nodes.rationale: Set 2026-06-11 after the owner's recurring complaint that explanations were too dense, skipped steps, and were not bagrut-focused. Every solution must satisfy all four: zero step-skipping, the topic-defining step highlighted, bagrut focus, and one $$...$$ line per step.
nodes.norm_label: בר האיכות — the four-rule quality bar for every solution

nodes.label: Gold-standard topic: math5/complex-numbers.ts
nodes.rationale: Rather than describing the bar abstractly, the guide names a concrete reference implementation (base + advanced complex-numbers paths) that every new topic must mimic in structure, tone and depth.

nodes.label: LearningPath 8-section structure (fixed order)
nodes.rationale: prerequisites → intuition → concepts → guidedExamples → pitfalls → practice → formulaSheet → comprehensionCheck. The TypeScript type in types.ts makes every section mandatory, so a missing section is a compile error rather than a silent content gap.

nodes.label: Zero step-skipping (אפס קפיצות)
nodes.rationale: Every computational step must be visible: (3+i)(2+i) shows 6+3i+2i+i², then the i²=−1 substitution, then 5+5i. A sentence that assumes knowledge not previously explained in the path fails the guide.

nodes.label: Atoms, not blocks (7 small concepts beat 3 big ones)
nodes.rationale: Each concept atom runs plain → formal → simplestExample → whyItWorks/diagrams. If an atom needs two separate ideas, split it. No formula is 'thrown in': formal always justifies or demonstrates it, or whyItWorks gives an analogy.
nodes.norm_label: atoms, not blocks (7 small concepts beat 3 big ones)

nodes.label: methodChoice — knowing WHEN to pick a method
nodes.rationale: Method selection is the actual missing skill — students know how to execute a method but not when to choose it, so every guided example opens with methodChoice and every step carries a `why` (the reasoning a student internalizes), not just an `action`.
nodes.norm_label: methodchoice — knowing when to pick a method

nodes.label: Progressive hint reveal + reviewIfStuck linkage
nodes.rationale: Hints go from gentle ('which quadrant is the point in?') to nearly-the-answer, revealed one at a time. Every reviewIfStuck.conceptId must match an existing ConceptAtom.id in the same path so the link scrolls to the right atom.

nodes.label: keyPoints ("לזכור") = triggers and traps, not formula repetition
nodes.rationale: Decided with the owner 2026-07-28 after Vieta's theorem appeared three times on one screen. The learn screen already shows each step's formula card plus the formulas section, so a keyPoint restating a formula 3cm above it is noise. Each bullet must answer one of: when does this fire, what does it save, what is the trap. 3-5 bullets, Hebrew prose, almost no $...$. Separately, LearnLevel auto-filters formulas already taught in a step, so formulas[] can stay complete for the global drawer without duplicating on screen.
nodes.norm_label: keypoints ("לזכור") = triggers and traps, not formula repetition

nodes.label: MCQ authoring: write the correct answer first (correct: 0)
nodes.rationale: Most readable in source, and the display layer already shuffles options deterministically by question id (lib/shuffle.ts → seededOrder), so the student never sees the correct answer in a fixed slot. Manually 'spreading' the correct position is redundant and harmful.
nodes.norm_label: mcq authoring: write the correct answer first (correct: 0)

nodes.label: Always double backslashes in LaTeX source strings
nodes.rationale: In JS strings a single backslash is swallowed as an escape, so \\sqrt / \\dfrac / \\text{cis} are required — including inside template literals.
nodes.norm_label: always double backslashes in latex source strings

nodes.label: Complex numbers: cis and degrees only, never e^{iθ} or radians
nodes.rationale: Mandated by the 5-unit syllabus: write 45°, 90°, 180°, 360° rather than π/4. Every result must also be hand-checked before saving — a single sign error burns the student's trust.
nodes.norm_label: complex numbers: cis and degrees only, never e^{iθ} or radians

nodes.label: No Hebrew inside math (learned in analytic geometry, 2026-06-10)
nodes.rationale: KaTeX performs no bidi, so \text{מרכז} or m_{משיק} render reversed ('זכרמ') plus console warnings. Hebrew labels go outside $...$ and subscripts use Latin letters ($m_r$).
nodes.norm_label: no hebrew inside math (learned in analytic geometry, 2026-06-10)

nodes.label: Bidi fixed at the rendering layer (2026-07-28) — no more content workarounds
nodes.rationale: The old rules ('never end a Hebrew sentence with $math$.', 'never open a line with a formula') existed because neutral punctuation flipped against math islands. The cause was removed: MathText now returns one element with dir="rtl" in both modes and every .katex is unicode-bidi:isolate, so a neutral run between two RTL sides resolves RTL per UAX#9 rule N1 — browser-verified. What remains forbidden is $$...$$ mid-prose-line, because remark-math hoists display math into its own block and orphans the following text; verify:content enforces it.
nodes.norm_label: bidi fixed at the rendering layer (2026-07-28) — no more content workarounds

nodes.label: MathText contract as stated in the style guide (one element, flex rule)
nodes.rationale: Both modes return one element (<span> inline, <div> block), which is what stops a display:flex container from decomposing a sentence into separate flex items — the bug that rendered the 'לזכור' box as three columns. A flex row containing MathText puts chat-md on an inner <div className="chat-md flex-1 min-w-0">, never on the flex container, because all .chat-md rules are descendant combinators.
nodes.norm_label: mathtext contract as stated in the style guide (one element, flex rule)

nodes.label: Diagram rules: DiagramSpec, custom raw SVG only, no fn: closures
nodes.rationale: A functionGraph closure crosses the server→client boundary and 500s the page in production, so curves must be drawn as static SVG. The SVG is inner content only (no wrapping <svg> tag), default viewBox 0 0 200 200, and captions pass through KaTeX so $...$ is allowed inside them.
nodes.norm_label: diagram rules: diagramspec, custom raw svg only, no fn: closures

nodes.label: Adding a new learning path (4-step procedure)
nodes.rationale: Create math5/<topic>.ts exporting a LearningPath, register it in index.ts under 'math5:<Hebrew topic name>' where the key must be byte-identical to the existing Lesson's topic so links resolve, then build/commit/push. The 'מסלול לימוד מ-0' banner then appears automatically on the existing topic page.
nodes.norm_label: adding a new learning path (4-step procedure)

nodes.label: Bagrut focus + Hebrew male-form, no decorative emoji
nodes.rationale: Content must say where a technique appears in the exam, which shortcut saves time, and what the grader wants to see — no textbook expansions beyond the exam. Hebrew is male-form (the owner identified as male), and no decorative emoji inside content since headings and components already carry icons.
nodes.norm_label: bagrut focus + hebrew male-form, no decorative emoji

nodes.label: Cognitive Map layer, Phase 1 (complex numbers)
nodes.rationale: The app knew HOW MANY answers were right at sub-topic resolution but not WHAT broke. This layer maps every answer to a named skill and a named misconception, runs local knowledge tracing, and emits one recommendation plus one Hebrew insight sentence — with zero new storage, zero API calls, and zero changes to verified content. Scope deliberately limited to math5 / מספרים מרוכבים, 5 sub-topics.

nodes.label: Super-principle: don't move state — derive it
nodes.rationale: All cognitive state is a pure function of the existing event log + a static catalog + the clock. This means no migration, no sixth store, no drift (state can never desync from evidence), full replay for synthetic students, free updates after every answer, and it is cheap: ≤1000 events × ~18 skills in one useMemo (<2ms). A separate bagrut-evidence-v1 store was explicitly rejected because it adds a second write path and a second sync target that can diverge.
nodes.norm_label: super-principle: don't move state — derive it

nodes.label: buildCognitiveState(events, catalog, now) — the single public entry point
nodes.rationale: Every module under lib/cognition/ is a pure function with no React, no localStorage and no internal Date.now() — the clock is always a `now` parameter. That is exactly what makes the layer fully testable and deterministic.
nodes.norm_label: buildcognitivestate(events, catalog, now) — the single public entry point

nodes.label: ResultEvent extension: kind, chosenIndex, hintUsed, optionCount
nodes.rationale: The single exception to 'derive, don't store': ResultEvent did not record WHICH distractor was chosen, so 'met the misconception and did not fall for it' was indistinguishable from 'never met it'. Four optional fields on an already-written event carry zero behavioral risk, unlike a separate evidence store. chosenIndex is the ORIGINAL index, not the shuffled one.
nodes.norm_label: resultevent extension: kind, chosenindex, hintused, optioncount

nodes.label: TopicCognitionMap catalog (content/cognition/)
nodes.rationale: The catalog lives in a separate file keyed by questionId rather than inside content/lessons/math5/complex-numbers.ts (4,160 lines, mathematically verified, concurrently modified). Result: zero risk to verified content, zero conflict with parallel sessions, and adding a topic is one file plus one registry line.

nodes.label: Skill type (id, prereqs, band)
nodes.rationale: SkillIds are namespaced strings ('cx.arg.quadrant') meant to be stable forever. `band` (easy/mid/hard) sets the BKT prior; `prereqs` is what makes the weakest-link diagnosis possible at all.

nodes.label: Misconception type (triggers, rootSkill, remedy, insight)
nodes.rationale: A misconception carries the skill it corrupts, an optional upstream rootSkill, the single Hebrew sentence shown on screen, a remedy pointing at an existing ladder destination, and `triggers` — (questionId, optionIndex) pairs where choosing that option IS the misconception. Open questions get optional `probes` checked through checkAnswer.

nodes.label: Complex-numbers skill prerequisite graph (18 planned / 22 built)
nodes.rationale: Resolution chosen at 18 skills (3-4 per sub-topic) rather than 8 (too coarse) or 30 (many skills would never accumulate evidence). Shipped at 22, each covered by at least one question, enforced by the gate.
nodes.norm_label: complex-numbers skill prerequisite graph (18 planned / 22 built)

nodes.label: BKT-lite knowledge tracing
nodes.rationale: Chosen over weighted accuracy because it (a) produces a probability so 'certainty' is a natural concept, (b) models guessing explicitly — critical when most questions are 4-option MCQ at 25% guess rate, (c) is a ~15-line incremental update. slip=0.10, transit=0.15, guess=1/optionCount for MCQ, 0.05 for machine-checked open, 0.15 for self-reported. hintUsed && correct skips the Bayes step and applies half transit, because correct-with-a-hint is not evidence of independent mastery; isReplay bumps guess to 0.5 since repeating a familiar question is weak evidence.

nodes.label: Forgetting decay (21-day half-life, applied at read time)
nodes.rationale: p_now = p0 + (p_last − p0)·2^(−Δdays/21). Applied on read rather than persisted, consistent with the derive-don't-store principle; the same 21-day recency weight w(t) is reused for misconception rates.
nodes.norm_label: forgetting decay (21-day half-life, applied at read time)

nodes.label: Misconception detection by lookup, not guessing
nodes.rationale: A chosen distractor index is looked up in the trigger table — no AI, no heuristics, no false positives, because a human already wrote in Hebrew what each distractor means; the layer only gives it an id. Answering a triggered question correctly counts as an 'opportunity' ('met it and didn't fall for it'). rate uses Laplace smoothing plus recency weighting; status walks resolved → fading → suspected → active.
nodes.norm_label: misconception detection by lookup, not guessing

nodes.label: Diagnose the weakest link in the prerequisite graph
nodes.rationale: Candidates are skills with evidence in the last 14 days in state fragile/developing; for each transitive prereq (depth ≤2) that is fragile, has confidence ≥0.35 and a gap p(child)−p(prereq) ≥0.15, a break is proposed. Largest gap wins, ties broken by graph depth then catalog order. This is what produces the target sentence: 'your problem isn't the complex roots — it's the quadrant fix in the argument before them.'
nodes.norm_label: diagnose the weakest link in the prerequisite graph

nodes.label: Next-best-step single arbitrator
nodes.rationale: Before this there were three separate voices — getResumePoint, dueItems, weakestSubTopics — and nothing adjudicated between them. Priorities: prereq-repair 100 × severity, misconception-drill 80 × weight, review-due 60, continue-ladder 40, consolidate 20, start 5; score = priority × urgency with deterministic tie-breaks. Critically the arbitrator never invents destinations — every href points at a screen that already exists.

nodes.label: Insight sentences from templates, not AI
nodes.rationale: Five Hebrew templates (prereq-break, misconception, fragile-recent, decayed, too-little). The last returns null on purpose: a diagnosis is not invented from 2 questions. Templates keep the whole feature at $0 Anthropic cost.
nodes.norm_label: insight sentences from templates, not ai

nodes.label: Separating "he is weak" from "we don't know"
nodes.rationale: SkillMastery carries `confidence` separately from `p`: confidence = 1 − exp(−effectiveN/3). Below the threshold the state is `unknown`, never `fragile`. This is the mechanism that prevents false accusations built on no evidence.
nodes.norm_label: separating "he is weak" from "we don't know"

nodes.label: MIN_CONFIDENCE raised to 0.5 (deviation from plan)
nodes.rationale: Testing showed 0.35 classified a student as `fragile` after just TWO answers. 0.5 sits between 2 and 3 observations. Biasing toward leniency is the expensive mistake — it turns 'we didn't measure' into 'you are weak at this'.

nodes.label: Merging prereq-repair with misconception-drill (deviation from plan)
nodes.rationale: When the strongest misconception sits ON the broken prereq they are the same conclusion at two resolutions. The first run had the headline blaming the argument while the button offered something else — a diagnosis and a prescription that contradict each other read as a bug even when both are correct. Now one candidate is emitted, phrased from the (more precise) misconception but carrying the prereq's priority. An invariant test locks this.
nodes.norm_label: merging prereq-repair with misconception-drill (deviation from plan)

nodes.label: hePrefix — Hebrew definite-article prefixing
nodes.rationale: Naive concatenation 'ב' + 'ההצגה' yields 'בההצגה'. Most skill titles are definite, so nearly every generated sentence would have been ungrammatical. A title opening with math gets a dash instead, matching the content style.

nodes.label: scripts/verify-cognition.ts — catalog integrity gate
nodes.rationale: Enforces: no orphan SkillId, no missing prereq, NO CYCLES in the graph, every trigger points at a real MCQ question and an in-range optionIndex that is NOT the correct answer (catching the 'marking a right answer as an error' class), no two misconceptions claiming the same distractor, every remedy resolving to an existing ladder rung, ≥10 misconceptions, every skill covered by a question. It explicitly cannot judge whether a misconception is the right reading of a distractor — that came from hand-reading all 186 distractor notes. Ships 0 errors, 14 warnings; the 14 are misconceptions whose triggers all sit on one question, which is an inventory limit and the next authoring worklist, not a bug.

nodes.label: scripts/test-cognition.ts — algorithm tests (fixed clock)
nodes.rationale: Written in the verify-review.ts house style (localStorage shim, fixed clock, PASS/FAIL). Covers BKT monotonicity, guess weighting (a single correct MCQ lifts p less than a correct open question), hint discounting, 42-day decay returning p halfway to prior, 2 observations → unknown not fragile, misconception rate 2/2 vs 2/9, and arbitrator determinism. 61/61 at phase 3, 68/68 after bagrut-part mapping.

nodes.label: Synthetic-student replay as the real proof
nodes.rationale: Three archetypes are replayed through the same pure function and asserted on the exact Hebrew sentence produced: the quadrant-confuser, the forgot-the-nth-root student, and the steady student — for whom the required output is insight = null and nextStep = continue-ladder, i.e. NOT inventing a problem.
nodes.norm_label: synthetic-student replay as the real proof

nodes.label: CognitiveInsightCard (phase 4 UI on /roadmap)
nodes.rationale: One component plus 3 wiring lines in app/roadmap/page.tsx, shown above the daily-review card. No new screen and no new navigation item. Live-verified on the public /roadmap (checkable without login): full card for the quadrant-confuser, no DOM node at all for the steady student, insight-without-CTA for legacy events lacking chosenIndex, correct bidi, no 375px horizontal overflow, 0 console errors, working deep-link.

nodes.label: Silence is a valid render (return null)
nodes.rationale: With no insight and no active misconception the component returns null. A panel that always has something profound to say about a student who answered 4 questions is a horoscope, and students recognize it.
nodes.norm_label: silence is a valid render (return null)

nodes.label: No competing CTA on /roadmap
nodes.rationale: /roadmap already has two buttons (daily review, resume), and next-step.ts may legitimately pick them; in that case the card shows only the REASON and draws no button. It renders a button only for prereq-repair and misconception-drill — the two kinds no other card offers. After seeing it in the browser, two headings both read 'הצעד הבא שלך', so the button became 'לתקן קודם — לפני שממשיכים', turning a collision into a sequence; the heading also now names the topic, since the page lists 10 topics.

nodes.label: Bagrut parts mapped to skills under `${questionId}-${partLabel}`
nodes.rationale: QuestionPartCard logs one event PER PART under a composite id like cx-bag-001-א — the bare question id never reaches results.ts, so any mapping keyed on cx-bag-001 would point at nothing. Explicit per-part mapping (26/26 by hand) is required because a bagrut question deliberately crosses skills (part א converts to polar, ב powers, ג returns to algebraic); a sub-topic fallback would both destroy that information and let a 5-part question emit ~35 observations and flood the tracer. A test locks it: 3 parts produce 6 observations, not 21.
nodes.norm_label: bagrut parts mapped to skills under `${questionid}-${partlabel}`

nodes.label: ResultEvent.selfReported — who graded the answer
nodes.rationale: false = lib/answer-check compared symbolically (or the AI judge); true = the student saw the solution and marked himself. guessFor prices them differently: 0.05 machine-graded, 0.25 self-reported (the generous grader in the app), 0.15 unknown (events written before the field existed). Without it a session of generous self-reporting would read as mastery. Applied to QuestionRunnerCard's two paths as well.

nodes.label: Results-log sync to Supabase by set union, not max-wins
nodes.rationale: learning_state.results already existed in supabase-learning-path.sql ('reserved for later phases'), so zero migration is needed. The roadmap store is a monotonically-advancing map where max-wins converges; the answer log is an append-only sequence, so the correct merge is set union keyed on (ts, source, questionId, subject, topic). The merge preserves unknown fields structurally — rebuilding field-by-field would have erased chosenIndex/selfReported/optionCount and blinded lib/cognition for every syncing student. test-sync.ts is 28/28, and its central test is that merge(a,b) equals merge(b,a), because order-dependent merging gives two devices two different grade predictions.
nodes.norm_label: results-log sync to supabase by set union, not max-wins

nodes.label: `repeat` is re-derived on merge, never merged
nodes.rationale: `repeat` means 'this was already answered before', but each device only knew its own history, so both rightly recorded 'first attempt' for the same question; a naive union would count both as measurements and inflate the predicted grade. Recomputing over the merged, sorted log is order-independent AND repairs flags that were wrong while devices were disconnected. The derived 'already counted' set is therefore not synced — it is rebuilt locally.
nodes.norm_label: `repeat` is re-derived on merge, never merged

nodes.label: 200KB payload guards (byte-identical skip + 15s debounce)
nodes.rationale: A full log is ~200KB of JSON against ~10KB for the map, and students are on phones. Two guards: skip the write entirely when the merged body is byte-identical to the previous one (visibilitychange and beforeunload fire right after a push and would otherwise re-upload the same 200KB), and debounce 4s → 15s while keeping an immediate flush on page exit. Defensively, the SELECT is `*` rather than a column list and a failed upsert retries without `results`, so a missing column on an old-schema table cannot take down the already-working map sync. recordResult now marks dirty, otherwise an answer only reached the server on the next unrelated write.

nodes.label: distractorNotes — 65 pre-written misconceptions being thrown away
nodes.rationale: complex-numbers.ts already had 65 MCQ questions all carrying distractorNotes — every distractor is an articulated, verified Hebrew misconception. When a student clicked distractor #2 the system displayed the note and logged category 'אחר', losing the misconception's identity. The signal was already in the click; only the display used it. Also relies on seededOrder(n, q.id) shuffling being deterministic while `selected` stays the ORIGINAL index, making chosenIndex a clean signal. Shipped: 46 misconceptions, 186 triggers, 103 mapped questions.
nodes.norm_label: distractornotes — 65 pre-written misconceptions being thrown away

nodes.label: ErrorCategory collapses to 'אחר' — why misconceptionId stays separate
nodes.rationale: ErrorCategory defaults to 'אחר' with manual re-tagging, and an incident is already documented where /errors announced '100% of your mistakes are of type other'. ErrorCategory is a taxonomy FOR THE USER; misconceptionId is a DIAGNOSTIC identifier. Merging them would reproduce exactly that collapse. A one-way misconceptionId → ErrorCategory mapping for display is fine later; a union is not.
nodes.norm_label: errorcategory collapses to 'אחר' — why misconceptionid stays separate

nodes.label: Five disconnected localStorage stores (audit)
nodes.rationale: results / roadmap-progress / mistakes / review / study-plan each keep their own key, and roadmap-sync only pushes roadmap and plan to Supabase — so results, mistakes and review (the diagnostic substrate) existed only on the current device. This audit is the reason the plan added results to sync later.
